newsitem.title: UK: Brit Midland to add to Boeing stable.
newsitem.headline: Brit Midland to add to Boeing stable.

text.p: British Midland, the airline which announced the biggest order for Airbus Industrie planes ever placed by a British company on Wednesday, said this did not signal a move away from its main supplier Boeing but that it would use both manufacturers in future.

Sir Michael Bishop, chairman of British Midland, told Reuters in an interview "We decided on a policy of having both Airbus and Boeing. We are not dropping Boeing and we will be adding more Boeing aircraft in future." This could be through leasing or buying second hand aircraft, he said. Bishop added that the group had decided to buy Airbus aircraft for the first time for a variety of reasons.
"In the past we've been almost exclusively customers of Boeing. But for technical and financial reasons we went for Airbus.
"The Airbus A321 (seating 196 people) was suited to our short haul routes and the financial terms were more favourable," said the British Midland chairman.

He added that the delivery of the first three aircraft from Airbus will be made a year from now and spread over five years. British Midland said the aircraft order responded to compound passenger growth of six to seven percent a year.
British Midland placed a $1 billion order for 20 Airbus aircraft. The chairman said the group will make a decision on engine manufacturers by July.
The fight for the engine order is between the Franco-American CFMI and the IAE consortia.
